title: How to structure a Gentleman split (volume & intensity)
summary: NH explains how to structure a training day in his Gentleman split, an upper/lower template with synergistic body-part grouping. Each day opens with 1-3 sets of strength work on a big compound, then optional back-off sets, then the bulk of tonnage done as supersets or giant sets of accessories, with the most important work first in a pyramid of priority.
claims: The Gentleman split is an upper/lower template with a body-part component, e.g. an upper day of chest, triceps and shoulders
Body-part splits are the worst type of program compared to the Gentleman split
The more advanced you become, the more flexibility you need in your program
Lower body days in typical upper/lowers waste tonnage; add traps, forearms, calves, back isolation, abs or even pull-ups to them
Plan a day by first listing the body parts to hit, then choosing the lifts

Always open the workout with strength work on a big compound movement pattern such as squat, deadlift, bench, good morning, overhead press, curl or dips, not a lateral raise, calf raise or leg extension
Do 1-3 sets of strength work; more than about four sets stops being max effort and becomes a mix of strength and back-off sets
Back-off sets follow strength work if needed and are an easy way to add tonnage because they replicate the movement
Grouping synergistic body parts means you stay warm after the opening lift and need few extra warm-up sets
Benching and squatting on the same day is not a Gentleman split; a full body or non-synergistic upper/lower mix cannot be one
Strength work is an appetizer, not something to kill yourself on; if you are cooked afterwards you programmed it wrong
Strength work and back-offs make up about 30-35% of the session's volume, but they drive progression the most
If short on time, do only the strength work and skip the rest
Structure the day as a pyramid: the most important work first, the least important isolation for muscles you don't care about last so it can be skipped
Lagging body parts trained at the end of the workout don't grow because those sets get skipped and aren't prioritised; whatever comes early progresses
Program accessories as giant sets or at least supersets; only the strength work and back-offs are normally not supersetted
He never supersets squats, deadlifts and bench with tonnage work, only with strength restoration work to stay warm
Bench can be supersetted with some movements without hurting performance; he supersets his back-off sets with pull-ups
Resting two minutes between sets of curls wastes tonnage; the biceps need rest but the rest of the body doesn't, so train other muscles meanwhile
With a big enough giant set of five exercises, you are fresh enough to restart the first exercise when the fifth is done, with no breaks
Never schedule a day without knowing what each exercise is for; program like a recipe, not by throwing ingredients in the pan
Accessories end up as 3-4 sets per body part per movement via supersets and make up most of the tonnage
Skipping accessories turns a Gentleman split into a minimalist template; the split is anti-minimalist
Don't program strength squats, back-off squats, front squats and paused squats in one day; repeating one pattern is worse than a bro split
Train quads, glutes and hamstrings together as a package on lower days
Example lower giant set: Romanian deadlift, shrugs with the same weight, calves, leg raises
The Gentleman split is essentially a modified Apollo-style template people have used for decades
If you can get away with doing less, do it; spend as little time in the gym as possible
A typical day for him is 1-3 strength sets plus 6-8 back-off, variation or accessory sets
Ease into giant sets gradually; jumping straight in will leave you cooked and you'll wrongly conclude the system is bad
A Gentleman split does not have to last 2-3 hours; switching to it shouldn't take you from one hour to three
Rotations create clone days hitting the same muscles with slight differences, effectively doubling the days in a program and helping avoid overuse injuries
exercises: opening strength lift; he does not superset it with tonnage work
in a giant set followed by shrugs with the same weight
hip hinge for hamstrings and posterior chain
